terms.gloss: be equivalent, mean the same, be worth the same
terms.grammar: verb phrase: valeō, valēre, valuī; with quod or atque for “as”
evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.13: quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 1.5.4: duo quae idem significant ac tantundem valent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of words, sums and things alike: valēre is to be worth and, of words, to mean (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending; with the dative
evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.13: verbum Latīnum pār Graecō (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: as good as, the equivalent of; as big as
terms.grammar: indeclinable noun, with the genitive; usually with esse or habēre
evidence: Cic. Pis. 52: ūnus ille diēs mihi immortālitātis instar fuit (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 2.15: instar montis equus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly a likeness: what something comes to, in worth or in size (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: just as much: the equivalent amount
terms.grammar: neuter of tantusdem, used as a noun; with quantum for “as”
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.3.201: tantundem dētur … quantum semper datum est (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat
phrases.english: we are looking for a Latin word equal to the Greek one, one that means the same

phrases.latin: ūnus ille diēs mihi immortālitātis instar fuit
phrases.english: that one day was worth immortality to me

sources: Lewis & Short: valeo · Lewis & Short: par · Lewis & Short: instar · Lewis & Short: tantusdem
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
